messages:
jamie: Heads up — seeing spikes in apiserver 5xx and controller-manager leader churn in eu-west1. etcd commit p95 ~250ms and several GPU attach timeouts. Provisioner is falling back to on-demand host pools, cost is climbing. Anyone already looking?

infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: eu-west1 apiserver 5xx rate 4.3% (5m), controller-manager leader flips=12 (15m), etcd_commit_ms p95=248ms. Recent rolling reboot on apiserver nodes at 01:12UTC. (inc: https://redwood.incidents/eu-west1/5023)

olivia: I'm pulling journal logs from the three apiserver VMs now. Quick glance: nvme_io_wait spikes during commit windows, a bunch of WAL fsyncs tied to compaction.

samir: Can we route new GPU provisioning to the Dedicated fallback pool while we triage? That should stop the attach failures from cascading to user-facing errors. Also consider temporarily throttling watch fanout — fewer open connections to apiserver.

jamie: +1 to fallback. samir, can you flip the routing rule? caroline can you prepare a short comms blurb for customers on impacted queues?

caroline: On it. Draft: "We're routing new GPU starts to reserved pools in eu-west while we investigate apiserver/connectivity instability. No action required from customers." Will post after we confirm the route. :memo:

samir: Routing change done — throttled provisioning to dedicated-fallback pool for eu-west1 (5m rollout). Observability: provisioning error rate dropping but apiserver still showing 5xx for some controlplane-heavy reconciles.

olivia: Found kube-apiserver logs showing frequent EPIPE and 'write: connection reset by peer' to the etcd endpoints during heavy compaction windows. NVMe GC + compaction IOPS => short stalls.

jamie: That matches the WAL fsync pattern. Two mitigations: 1) reduce compaction I/O pressure (tune compactor) 2) increase controller-manager lease/renewDeadline so leader flips less often. Thoughts?

samir: For immediate relief do (1) and (2). I can patch controller-manager flags to renewDeadline=15s (currently 10s) and leaseDuration=60s (currently 30s) for controller-manager so transient delays don't trigger re-elections.

olivia: I'll throttle etcd compactor: bump --max-backoff and reduce compaction frequency for now. Command I plan to run: 

```
kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment etcd-compactor --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"compactor","args":["--compact-interval=15m","--max-backoff=5s"]}]}}}}'
```

samir: And patch for controller-manager: 

```
kubectl -n kube-system set env deployment/controller-manager --containers=controller-manager --env="KUBE_CONTROLLER_MANAGER_ARGS=--leader-elect=true --leader-elect-lease-duration=60s --leader-elect-renew-deadline=15s"
```

jamie: Wait on the env patch until olivia confirms compactor patch applied. We don't want to change election settings while compactor still spiking writes.

olivia: Compactor patched and rolling. Observability shows lower nvme_io_wait on compactor hosts after ~90s. apiserver 5xx dropped from 4.3% -> 1.2% over the last minute.

samir: Ok rolling the controller-manager lease adjustments now (small canary to one replica first). If leader flips stop, we'll promote to all.

infra-bot: ACTION: controller-manager env patch applied to replica-0 canary at 5023456798. Monitoring leader flips.

caroline: Cost note: fallback to dedicated pool increased hourly spend by ~18% last 45m. I'll put a rough estimate in the incident ticket.

jamie: Good catch. We'll keep routing fallback until metrics stable for 30m. Olivia/samir — after things calm down, let's run a short postmortem focusing on: NVMe compactor scheduling, apiserver WAL fsync patterns, and whether we need IO QoS for etcd VMs.

olivia: Agreed. Also want to test moving etcd WAL to separate NVMe partition with higher IOPS or throttle compactor more gracefully in sustained compaction windows.

samir: Also adding follow-up: enable in-flight KV cache to reduce watch fanout load during peaks (Optimize routing + cache).

jamie: Thanks all. I'll update the incident with current mitigation, cost impact, and the follow-up tasks. Reopen if we see new spikes. :white_check_mark:
